title: Request maturity & risk classifier for hosted chat/streaming/toolcall intake
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create an automated maturity-and-risk classifier to sit in the Hosted API intake pipeline for enterprise feature requests that touch chat, streaming, tool/function calling, or structured outputs. The classifier will synthesize signals (customer maturity, SLA ask, data residency, required tool integrations, schema complexity, predicted token cost) to assign requests into: QuickShip (low friction), Needs Design (moderate), HighRisk (requires legal/security and Dedicated/Private discussion), and Blocked (non-starter until pre-reqs met). This ticket scopes the rubric, the intake form changes, and the first-pass rules for automatic assignment and routing into PM/SE queues.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented rubric with scoring for at least 7 signals (customer maturity, SLA percentiles, data residency, PII handling, tool integration count, structured-output complexity, estimated cost per 1k tokens) exists in Confluence and is reviewed by Security and Solutions Eng.
2) Intake form updated to collect the required signals (tenant maturity, compliance flags, expected traffic, schema size).
3) Prototype classifier implemented as rule-based engine in intake service that automatically tags new requests and routes to QuickShip/Needs Design/HighRisk/Blocked queues.
4) Automated unit tests for each rule and E2E smoke test for routing added to intake CI.
5) Pilot run with 30 historical requests: classifier accuracy >= 80% vs. manual historical labels, and false-negative rate for HighRisk < 5%.
6) Runbook for manual override, appeals, and SE handoff documented.
decisions: Use a hybrid approach: start with deterministic rule-based scoring (transparent for audit) and instrument telemetry to drive a future ML model (6-9 months).

Blocker threshold set conservatively: any request with 'requires_eu_data_residency' AND 'requests_streaming_with_toolcalls' -> HighRisk automatically. This reduces missed-compliance cases at cost of more manual triage overhead initially.
Estimate key signals in intake by converting free-text traffic expectations into percentile bands (low/med/high) to keep form simple for customers.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-3): docs + intake form + rule engine prototype behind feature flag; run pilot on a subset of enterprise orgs and internal SE intake. Phase 2 (week 4-6): integrate routing to PM/SE queues, add manual override UI, monitor telemetry and false positives; iterate rules. Phase 3 (week 7-12): open to all enterprise signups, collect labeled data for ML model R&D; revisit thresholds and reduce conservative blocks where safe.
notes: Trade-offs: conservative blocking reduces compliance risk but increases manual triage load — acceptable for initial rollout. Long-term goal is to convert high-signal rules into ML classifiers to reduce maint burden. Need to align with Privacy and Legal on the 'customer_maturity' signal interpretation to avoid discrimination concerns.
